featured_videos.editorial_title: Project 20: Losing the Regain | Staying Low Carb While Traveling for Work #weightloss
featured_videos.commentary: The comments say it all. people aren't just watching the weight loss, they're watching *you*. And honestly, that's what makes Project 20 different from every other transformation video out there. DeeDee's showing the real part nobody talks about: regain happens to almost everyone, and staying consistent while traveling for work is where carnivore and low-carb actually gets tested. Her community isn't just cheering the scale victories (though they are), they're holding themselves accountable alongside her. That's the ripple effect. When someone shows up and says "I passed the pizza," it gives the person watching permission to do the same thing tomorrow at their hotel dinner.

featured_videos.title: Why Muscle Meat Alone Is Not Enough For Your Heart (The Glycine Fix)
featured_videos.creator: Maurice Daher
featured_videos.editorial_title: Why Muscle Meat Alone Is Not Enough For Your Heart (The Glycine Fix)
featured_videos.commentary: Maurice just dropped something most carnivore influencers have been quietly sidestepping. You've got folks like Chaffee and Baker thriving on muscle meat alone, but as one commenter nailed it, maybe some people are just genetically wired differently or they're not measuring what's actually happening under the hood. The glycine-to-methionine imbalance isn't hype. it's basic amino acid biochemistry, and your arterial walls are literally made of collagen. If you're eating nothing but steak and ground beef, you're probably leaving connective tissue, bone broth, and slow-cooked shank on the table. The good news is it's a simple fix: a cup of broth daily or 3-5g glycine powder before bed isn't complicated, and a bunch of people in the comments are already running their own experiments on sleep and homocysteine. Worth trying for 30 days and actually tracking it.

featured_videos.title: Am I a Carnivore Hypocrite?
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.commentary: This hits different because it's not really about the popcorn. it's about permission. The community's getting it: you can run a carnivore business *and* exist in a non-carnivore world without being a sellout. That contradiction people are pointing out? That's just life. You're not converting the theater, you're giving people who *want* options a place to find them. The pushback on "hypocrisy" misses the whole point. nobody expects you to burn down the system from the inside, just to be honest about your choices and respect that others make theirs.

featured_videos.title: 21 Days Zero Carb Diet Plan Challenge | Lose 8 Kgs Weight In 21 Days (In Hindi) | Let's Go Healthy
featured_videos.creator: Let's Go Healthy
featured_videos.editorial_title: 21 Days Zero Carb Diet Plan Challenge | Lose 8 Kgs Weight In 21 Days (In Hindi) | Let's Go Healthy
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here are telling. One viewer mentions hitting a weight plateau and wondering if a strict 21-day push is just the reset they need, while another's asking the real question about sustainability. Here's the thing: rapid weight loss plans work best as circuit breakers when you're genuinely stuck, not as a forever protocol. If you're considering something like this, the math matters less than whether you can actually stick with it beyond day 21. The people seeing real results in the comments aren't just following a chart, they're combining the plan with consistency and effort. That's always been the missing piece in these challenges.

featured_videos.editorial_title: Every Benefit of The Carnivore Diet Explained in 12 Minutes
featured_videos.commentary: Sean nails something important here that doesn't get said enough: carnivore isn't a trend or a hack, it's a reset. The comments tell the real story. People showing up at 72 with steady energy, reversing problems that "healthy eating" couldn't touch, gaining mental clarity they'd forgotten was possible. That's not marketing talk, that's what happens when you stop fighting your biology. The book recommendations and sprinting success stories in the thread show what we're seeing across the board, especially with our core audience of women over 45 looking for weight loss and energy stability. What's worth noting is how many people mention the simplicity piece, the food noise quieting down, the elimination of digestive chaos. That's the part that keeps people going long-term, not willpower.

featured_videos.title: I Make These Carnivore Chips Every Week
featured_videos.creator: Meet Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: I Make These Carnivore Chips Every Week
featured_videos.commentary: What's wild about this video is how the comments keep circling back to one thing: you don't need the gadgets. Someone's talking about a rolling pin replacing their pie baker, another person's air frying Parmesan, and the top comment is basically "I actually make your recipes because I'm not hunting down some specialized equipment." That's the real win here. On carnivore, we're already stripping things down to the basics, and this just proves that applies to your kitchen too. If you've been thinking snacking on carnivore means beef jerky and nothing else, this is a gentle reminder that texture and variety live in your pantry already, not in a catalog order.
